comparison.approach: four semantic shards plus targeted per-file diagnostics inside distributed-faults
comparison.correctness: high; coverage is unchanged and every distributed fault test is still executed
comparison.robustness: highest practical option with current tooling because the failing file is emitted as a GitHub annotation even when job logs are unavailable
comparison.latency: distributed-fault files run sequentially during diagnosis, modestly increasing that shard latency but not runner count

comparison.qa: next red run will name each failing distributed-fault test file explicitly through ::error annotations

whyItWon: The semantic sharding already proved the defect is confined to distributed-faults. Adding per-file annotations inside that single shard gives exact fault localization without the resource cost and workflow sprawl of one runner per test file. It is the strongest balance of correctness, robustness, latency, resource use, and regression risk for the current failure mode.
failuresAndLessons: DIG Node QA #137 proved the semantic shards work: syntax-check, queue-core, worker-reliability, and synthetic-sandboxes passed while distributed-faults failed.
A subsystem-level red result is not yet enough when Actions logs are inaccessible; the CI must surface the failing filename in structured annotations.
Diagnostic instrumentation should not alter production semantics while the root cause remains unknown.
Temporary sequential execution inside the failing shard is preferable to multiplying runners because it preserves bounded resource use and makes every failing file visible in one run.
Once the root cause is fixed and all shards are green, the diagnostic loop can remain as low-cost observability or be returned to parallel node --test execution if latency becomes material.
nextGate: read the per-file distributed-fault annotations from the next Node QA run, repair the exact failing test or production invariant with a regression test, then require all five gates green before any real Qubes worker campaign
